clusters.name: Know number names and the count sequence

standards.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens, demonstrating knowledge of the number sequence.
standards.ccssText: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

standards.description: Count forward beginning from any given number up to 100 without needing to start over from 1.
standards.ccssText: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

standards.description: Write numerals from 0 to 20 and represent a quantity of objects with the corresponding written numeral, including 0 for an empty set.
standards.ccssText: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

clusters.name: Count to tell the number of objects

standards.description: Understand that counting tells how many objects are in a set, that the last number said is the total, and that each successive number is one more.
standards.ccssText: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

subStandards.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.
Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.
Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

standards.description: Count up to 20 objects arranged in various configurations and count out a specified number of objects when given a number from 1 to 20.
standards.ccssText: Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.

standards.description: Identify whether one group of objects is greater than, less than, or equal to another group using matching and counting strategies.
standards.ccssText: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.

standards.description: Compare two written numerals between 1 and 10 and determine which is greater or less.
standards.ccssText: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

clusters.name: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from

standards.description: Represent addition and subtraction using objects, fingers, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, or equations.
standards.ccssText: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.

standards.skillName: Addition and Subtraction Word Problems within 10
standards.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems and add or subtract within 10 using objects or drawings.
standards.ccssText: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

standards.description: Break apart numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way, recording each decomposition with a drawing or equation.
standards.ccssText: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

standards.description: Find the number that makes 10 when added to any number from 1 to 9, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.
standards.ccssText: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

standards.description: Add and subtract within 5 with fluency.
standards.ccssText: Fluently add and subtract within 5.

domains.name: Number and Operations in Base Ten

clusters.name: Work with numbers 11–19 to gain foundations for place value

standards.skillName: Teen Numbers as Ten Plus Ones
standards.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 as ten ones and some additional ones, recording each with a drawing or equation.
standards.ccssText: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

standards.description: Describe measurable attributes such as length or weight for objects, and identify multiple measurable attributes of a single object.
standards.ccssText: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

standards.description: Directly compare two objects with a common measurable attribute and describe which has more or less of that attribute.
standards.ccssText: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.

clusters.name: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category

standards.description: Sort objects into given categories, count the objects in each category, and order the categories by count.
standards.ccssText: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.

clusters.name: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres)

standards.description: Name shapes found in the real world and describe their positions using spatial terms such as above, below, beside, and next to.
standards.ccssText: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

standards.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of how they are oriented or what size they are.
standards.ccssText: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

standards.description: Identify whether a shape is two-dimensional (flat) or three-dimensional (solid).
standards.ccssText: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

clusters.name: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes

standards.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes of different sizes and orientations using informal language about their similarities, differences, parts, and attributes.
standards.ccssText: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

standards.description: Model real-world shapes by building them from components such as sticks and clay, and by drawing shapes.
standards.ccssText: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

standards.description: Join simple shapes together to form larger shapes.
standards.ccssText: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes. For example, "Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?"
